events.title: Rouen burned
events.source: Travellers' talk among the war news.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: And one more thing, my lord, though it's far from here: Northmen came up the Seine in their ships in May and burned Rouen, and the monasteries along the river. With every lord in the kingdom marching to fight his brothers, there was no one to stop them.

events.title: Bishop Gunhard killed at Nantes
events.source: The clergy of the diocese; Ermenald raises it himself, shaken.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: My lord, the clergy are speaking of nothing else. On the feast of Saint John, Northmen sailed up the Loire to Nantes. The town was full of people for the feast; they broke into the cathedral while the bishop was saying Mass, and killed him at the altar, with the clergy and the people who had taken refuge there. Then they carried off the rest as captives. At the altar, my lord. Is nowhere holy to these men?

knows: Churches and monasteries along the rivers are beginning to ask where to send their relics and treasures for safety.

events.title: Paris taken

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the Northmen have taken Paris. A fleet came up the Seine in March, beat the men the king sent against them, and hanged their prisoners where the king's army could see. They were in the city at Easter. King Charles paid them seven thousand pounds of silver to go away, and they went, laden. Seven thousand pounds, my lord. That's a lesson the Northmen won't forget: Frankish kings pay.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: The churches and abbeys about Paris have given up their plate toward it, my lord, and the bishops are not quiet about who failed to defend them. And the count's officer says the kingdom is to find a share of the sum: sixpence from every manse. For us that is {levy_845}.

knows: Contemporaries call him King Charles; nobody here calls him 'the Bald'.
The seven thousand pounds were raised from the king and the people of the land; the church paid a large share, and part was paid in gold.

events.title: Tours sacked; the relics of Saint Martin

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the Northmen from the Loire have burned Tours, and the great church of Saint Martin with it. The canons got out in time, they say, and carried the saint's body away with them, inland, to Auxerre.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: My lord, Saint Martin himself, at Auxerre! A day's hard ride from here. And it isn't only Tours: churches all along the rivers are sending their treasures and relics inland, looking for safe hands. I've been asked whether you would take some into your keeping. I said I would ask.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: What is offered is modest, my lord: a small reliquary of a lesser saint, with some books and altar plate from a small community on the river. They ask only that it be kept dry and honoured.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.when: (rank == 2 or rank <= 1) and relic_refuge_offer and rank < 3
script.text: They remembered what you said after Nantes, my lord. What is offered is a church treasury, larger than I expected for a house like ours, and a few monks who come with it to keep the offices. They would eat at your table.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: What is offered befits your standing, my lord: a church treasury, and a few monks who come with it to keep the offices. They would eat at your table.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: My lord, for a man of your standing they speak of a major shrine. Saint Martin himself goes to Auxerre and will stay there; but there are other great relics looking for walls, and yours are strong enough to ask for one.

knows: Accepting brings church favour, prestige, pilgrims and their gifts; it also brings monks to feed if a treasury comes, higher visibility, thieves and greedy neighbours, and once the Northmen reach Burgundy a treasure is a target.
If the treasure were ever lost or stolen the church would not forgive it. When the danger passes the owners will ask for it back.

They will send men and a cart at Easter if you say yes.

You are not a young man, my lord. Nobody expects you in the front rank. A captain, and the men, or your own counsel at his side from behind the line: those are the ways.

events.title: Robert the Strong is dead

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, Count Robert is dead. He caught the Northmen and the Bretons at Brissarthe, in Anjou, after they'd burned Le Mans, and penned them up in a stone church. It was blazing hot; he took off his helmet and his mail to rest, and they came bursting out. He was cut down before he could arm himself. Count Ranulf of Poitou took an arrow there too and died of it. The best fighter in the kingdom, my lord, killed for want of a helmet. Autun has no count again.

events.title: The monks of Saint-Philibert come to Tournus

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the king has given the abbey at Tournus to the monks of Saint-Philibert, the ones who fled the Northmen on the Loire all those years ago. They've been wandering for forty years, they say. Now they'll be our neighbors on the Saône, with the king's protection and whatever lands came with the abbey. A great house, so close; that will change things hereabouts.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: My lord, they will pass near us on the last stage from the Auvergne, carrying the body of Saint Philibert himself. Their abbot has asked the lords along the road for help. It would be a great honor to receive a saint, and the monks would never forget it.

script.speaker: chaplain
script.text: And they know your name already, my lord. The house that offered the river churches shelter when nobody else would: that is how their abbot's letter puts it. They are coming to us warmly.

knows: Hospitality, carts and guides, and an armed escort each earn the abbey's goodwill; all three together make a lasting friend and patron.
A few displaced families have drifted east with the monks and could be settled on vacant manses.
One of the monks, Ermentarius, wrote the history of their wanderings and complains bitterly that lords paid tribute instead of fighting.
The abbey will be a large landholder and a competitor for land, labour and pilgrims.

events.title: Victory at Saucourt

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, good news for once. Young King Louis, the old emperor Charles's grandson, caught a great band of Northmen at Saucourt, up in the Vimeu near the sea, and slaughtered them. Thousands dead, they say, though you know how they say. The Franks across the Rhine are already singing a song about it. It's proof the Northmen can be beaten in the open field, my lord, when a king will stand and fight.

events.title: Paris besieged

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the Northmen have come back to the Seine in strength, hundreds of ships, and they are at Paris. Count Odo holds the city, and Bishop Gozlin with him, on their island between the two bridges. They say the Northmen offered to pass by if the bridges were opened, and Odo refused them. Now they are building engines. Paris cannot hold out forever, and no one is coming: the emperor is in Italy.

stages.title: Seven hundred pounds, and the Yonne

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, he paid them. The emperor had the Northmen surrounded on Montmartre with the whole army of Italy and Burgundy at his back, and he did not fight. Seven hundred pounds of silver, and leave to go up the Yonne and winter in Burgundy, which has not been loyal enough to suit him. Paris is disgusted; Count Odo is said to have defied the arrangement to the emperor's face. And we are the country they have been given leave to winter in.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: You said it in front of the army, my lord, and the men who heard you have not forgotten. Odo's people least of all.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: The emperor's answer to you was short, my lord: you are trapped in Burgundy with me. He will send them regardless, but he backs you to contain them: men, coin, authority to raise the region's levies, and a commission. A great chance, and a great risk.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: And to you he leaves the choice, my lord. He will not punish Burgundy at the cost of his best man in it. Spend your favour and he sends them elsewhere; or take them on, with imperial backing.

events.title: The Northmen in Burgundy

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, they are coming up the Yonne. The emperor's own safe-conduct in their hands, and they are coming to winter on us. They have sat down before Sens and mean to take it. Everything outside the walls between here and the Yonne is theirs for the taking until spring.

knows: The band is the core of the force that besieged Paris: a thousand to three thousand veterans practised at siege work. A field battle against the whole army is suicide.

What a smaller force can do: hit foraging parties; empty the villages, hide stores, drive livestock into the woods, break bridges and block fords; night raids on the camp; ambushes at crossings; burn the beached ships (very high risk).
Poisoning the camp's stores needs someone inside; if it becomes known the church condemns it and renown suffers.
Plague-fouled cloth as 'loot' would do nothing to the enemy and might sicken the household that handled it.

They will go back to Paris for their silver when the roads dry. Until then we are still in their larder.

events.title: Burgundy cleared

script.speaker: steward
script.text: My lord, the marquis came on the Northmen's camp at Argenteuil on the Armançon before dawn, in December, and broke it. Those who got away he caught again near Saint-Florentin, and the rest are back in the Seine valley with nothing to show for the winter. Burgundy is clear of them. For the first time since the emperor sent them up the Yonne, there is not a Northman camped on our country.

script.speaker: steward
script.text: The marquis has a long memory for who rode and who did not, my lord.
